Sam (SI-AnchorPoint): hitting a blocker during AnchorPoint's air-gapped deployment: two nodes intermittently fail when pulling the marketplace image. Errors alternate between `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and `denied: requested access to the resource is denied`. They use an enterprise proxy (Squid) with SSL bump. Need registry endpoints, CA distribution advice, and any temporary bypass options.

Priya (Partnerships): looping in platform + solutions. @Ibrahim any registry/CIDR to share? @Carla can you outline the image auth flow?

Ibrahim (Eng-Platform): Registry host: registry.market.redwood.ai (443). Egress IPs we publish are 52.12.34.56 and 52.12.34.57 (recommend whitelisting outbound 443 to those). We also have a token auth endpoint at https://auth.market.redwood.ai/token.
Common issues with SSL-bumping proxies: the node/container runtime verifies cert chain against its CA store; if proxy intercepts TLS you must install the proxy CA into the runtime cert dir. For containerd: `/etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.market.redwood.ai/ca.crt`. Example: 
```
sudo mkdir -p /etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.market.redwood.ai
sudo cp company-proxy-ca.crt /etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.market.redwood.ai/ca.crt
sudo systemctl restart containerd
```
If kubelet/docker is involved, ensure the same CA is present for each runtime.

Carla (Solutions): For the `denied` error, confirm credentials. Kubernetes nodes typically need an imagePullSecret or a node-level credential. If the proxy rewrites auth headers, pulls to our token endpoint will 401. Two short-term options: 1) we can temporarily add the customer's NAT IP to a short allowlist so images can be pulled without proxy auth, or 2) we can provide a base64-encoded `dockerconfigjson` for them to use as imagePullSecret. Also check whether their proxy allows CONNECT to auth.market.redwood.ai:443.

Sam (SI-AnchorPoint): They tried adding the company root CA to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and ran `update-ca-certificates`, but containerd still rejects the cert. Logs show containerd referencing `/etc/containerd/certs.d` only.

Ibrahim (Eng-Platform): Right, OS-level CA isn't always picked up by container runtimes. Need to copy the pem into the containerd certs.d path and restart containerd. If they're using CRI-O or containerd shim, path differs. Also confirm systemd env for proxy (e.g. /etc/systemd/system/containerd.service.d/http-proxy.conf). Example drop-in: 
```
[Service]
Environment="HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128" "HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128" "NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost,registry.market.redwood.ai"
```

Nina (Customer Success): Customer requested a 45m deep-dive today at 14:30 CET. Can we get at least one infra engineer on the call?

Priya (Partnerships): I'll be on the call. @Ibrahim can you join? Carla?

Carla (Solutions): I can take the call too. Quick checklist to run before we join: 1) `openssl s_client -connect registry.market.redwood.ai:443 -showcerts` (confirm chain), 2) `ls -la /etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.market.redwood.ai`, 3) `journalctl -u containerd -u kubelet --since "1h" | tail -n 200` for auth failures, 4) try `curl -v --proxy '' https://auth.market.redwood.ai/token` from a node to avoid proxy.

ops-bot: allowlist-request: temporary allowlist window requested for IP 203.0.113.45 to egress 443 -> pending approval.

Sam (SI-AnchorPoint): They cannot run curl w/o going through the proxy (managed infra). Would prefer the temporary allowlist approach.

Ibrahim (Eng-Platform): We can open a 2-hour window for their NAT IP 203.0.113.45 from 2026-05-10T13:00Z to 2026-05-10T15:00Z. ops-bot will apply and notify.

ops-bot: allowlist-update: 203.0.113.45 allowed to registry.market.redwood.ai:443 from 2026-05-10T13:00Z to 2026-05-10T15:00Z.

Sam (SI-AnchorPoint): Thanks. Can you also share a sample imagePullSecret so we can preconfigure the k8s manifests?

Carla (Solutions): Sample secret (replace JSON key): 
```
echo '{"auths":{"registry.market.redwood.ai":{"auth":"BASE64_JSON_KEY"}}}' > ~/.docker/config.json
kubectl create secret generic reg-secret --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=~/.docker/config.json --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
```
Note: for managed node pools where nodes pull images directly, they may need node-level kubelet container runtime credentials instead of pod secrets.

Priya (Partnerships): Call confirmed 14:30 CET. Action items: Ibrahim to prepare allowlist, Carla to draft pull-secret example and diagnostics checklist, Sam to collect containerd logs and cert paths from customer.

Sam (SI-AnchorPoint): Got it. I'll bring logs and the output of `openssl s_client` to the call. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Nina (Customer Success): Customer expects resolution today; thanks everyone.

Ibrahim (Eng-Platform): I'll join and be ready to toggle the allowlist when they confirm readiness.

Priya (Partnerships): Perfect, see you on the call. :calendar:
